items.streamTitle: Macaque reaching habits reflected both learned value and persistent spatial bias
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports study found that repeated reaching choices in macaques were shaped by both learned reward values and enduring spatial preferences. The result argues against interpreting habitual behavior as only a value calculation or only motor repetition. Multiple learning processes can produce the same repeated choice pattern.

items.streamTitle: Germany and Ukraine expanded defense production agreements covering drones, interceptors, radar, and software
items.streamSummary: During Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Kyiv visit, Germany announced additional military aid and multiple industrial agreements with Ukrainian partners, including air-defense and drone technologies. The commitments show deeper defense-industrial integration, not completed capability. Delivery timelines, production throughput, and operational performance remain the important follow-on outcomes.

items.streamTitle: North Korea's hypersonic drill produced competing claims about tracking and interceptability
items.streamSummary: Reuters reported a North Korean hypersonic missile drill that state media said demonstrated deterrent reliability. South Korea disputed North Korean claims that regional militaries failed to track the missile and said its defenses could detect and intercept the tested system. The launch is observed evidence; performance and deterrence claims remain contested assessments.

items.streamTitle: Explicit belief state improved long-horizon agent consistency in PoS benchmarks
items.streamSummary: PoS is a preprint framework that maintains explicit beliefs and unresolved requirements for long-running agents. Reported benchmarks showed better execution and diagnosis than comparison methods. The result supports structured state management, but remains benchmark evidence; production reliability still depends on how accurately the state representation reflects external reality.

items.streamTitle: Most clinical SHAP studies omitted details needed to reproduce their explanations
items.streamSummary: A review of 100 clinical SHAP studies found major reporting gaps: most did not specify the computation algorithm and nearly all omitted reference-population details. Those choices can materially change explanations. The result is a reproducibility warning rather than a claim that SHAP is unusable; explanation methods need the same implementation transparency expected of other analytical procedures.

items.streamTitle: CompMat-Bench used deterministic scientific calculations to expose agent reasoning failures
items.streamSummary: CompMat-Bench created reproducible computational-materials tasks with known numerical ground truth. Scientific agents performed worse on longer workflows and with less guidance, and many failures reflected scientific reasoning rather than simple software misuse. The benchmark is valuable because it grades against independent calculations instead of an agent's own explanation.

items.streamTitle: Body-satisfaction prediction relied on different multimodal signals across cultures
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports study modeled body satisfaction using multimodal social-media information and found that predictive features differed across Western and East Asian participants. The result shows why a single global model can hide culturally specific relationships. Predictive features are not automatically causal mechanisms, and transfer across populations requires direct testing.

items.streamTitle: Profession-specific agent personas increased cost without consistently improving accuracy
items.streamSummary: A preprint compared detailed profession-specific agent profiles with simpler instructions. The richer prompts cost roughly 2.2–4.5 times more per successful call in the reported study without delivering a consistent accuracy advantage. The result suggests that task information and tools may matter more than elaborate role-play. Generalization beyond the tested tasks remains uncertain.

items.streamTitle: Supervisor incivility correlated with exhaustion and withdrawal, especially under higher power distance
items.streamSummary: A cross-sectional workplace study linked supervisor incivility with emotional exhaustion and withdrawal and found stronger relationships for some employees higher in power-distance orientation. The modeled mediation is theoretically plausible but not causally identified because variables were measured at the same time. Longitudinal or experimental evidence is needed before treating the pathway as established.

items.streamTitle: A lung-cancer vaccine moved immune markers without producing objective tumor responses
items.streamSummary: A phase I lung-cancer vaccine study reported immunological changes but no objective tumor responses. Early-phase studies can be valuable for safety and biological activity, yet those intermediate signals should not be upgraded into evidence of clinical efficacy. The result is a clear example of why proxy and final outcomes must remain distinct.

items.streamTitle: The Army created a Robotics Technician warrant-officer specialty for sustaining autonomous systems
items.streamSummary: The U.S. Army graduated its first Robotics Technician warrant officers under MOS 390A. The specialty formalizes expertise for integrating, operating, and sustaining robotic systems across units. This is an institutional milestone rather than evidence of platform effectiveness. Workforce design, maintenance burden, and unit-level integration will determine whether autonomous systems become durable capability.

items.streamTitle: Apple said AI agents make Full Disk Access riskier and announced stronger permission controls
items.streamSummary: Apple announced plans for additional safeguards around macOS Full Disk Access, noting that increasingly capable AI agents raise the stakes of giving applications access to files, mail, messages, and browsing history. The announcement is a platform-security change rather than evidence that the new controls reduce incidents. It supports least-privilege design and explicit user authorization for powerful agents.

items.streamTitle: Pentagon Lightfish pilots used persistent autonomous boats for maritime border surveillance
items.streamSummary: Reuters reported that solar-powered Lightfish vessels were providing persistent maritime surveillance with sensors feeding military and border-security networks. Officials cited hundreds of detections, apprehensions, and turnbacks in an average month, but those outcomes were not experimentally attributable to the boats alone. The pilot demonstrates operational use; marginal effectiveness and cost-effectiveness still need comparison.

items.streamTitle: English-to-Arabic depression detection showed a large transfer gap
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports study found very strong English depression-text classification but substantially weaker transfer to Arabic, including more false negatives. The result is a clear warning against treating multilingual deployment as a translation problem alone. Language, culture, data distribution, and class-specific errors need direct validation before high-stakes use.

items.streamTitle: Multimodal narratives improved classification of healthcare-worker stress profiles
items.streamSummary: A longitudinal healthcare-worker study used multimodal features from recorded narratives to classify stress-related profiles. The combined model outperformed language alone, indicating that information was distributed across modalities. The result supports multimodal measurement, but predictive accuracy does not establish that the inferred profiles are stable causal types or transport unchanged to other populations.

items.streamTitle: A clinical-board LLM showed useful support but only partial agreement and repeatability
items.streamSummary: A prospective clinical study evaluated an LLM during 100 real specialist-board cases. The system often generated relevant recommendations, but complete agreement with specialists was only around half in consensus-rated cases and repeated evaluations did not always produce the same result. The evidence supports decision support, not autonomous clinical authority or demonstrated patient benefit.

items.streamTitle: Majority-group preference emerged later in development rather than appearing uniformly in infancy
items.streamSummary: A Nature Human Behaviour study compared majority-versus-minority preferences across infants, preschoolers, and adults. Infants did not show a reliable majority preference, while stronger preferences appeared in some older groups. The result argues against treating attraction to numerical majorities as an invariant early bias. Developmental stage and social meaning matter.

items.streamTitle: Visual prompts immediately changed gait mechanics in multiple sclerosis
items.streamSummary: A controlled study found that brief visual prompts could immediately alter selected gait mechanics among people with multiple sclerosis. The effect shows that movement patterns were modifiable in the moment, but the study did not establish lasting adherence, reduced falls, or improved daily functioning. Immediate biomechanical change and long-term clinical benefit remain separate outcomes.

items.streamTitle: Decentralized Q-learning improved traffic flow in simulation
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports study used decentralized reinforcement-learning agents to control simulated traffic intersections. The agents improved travel time, queueing, and throughput relative to tested baselines. These are simulation results, not field evidence. Sensor errors, driver adaptation, communications failures, and unusual events remain important before operational deployment.

items.streamTitle: Multimodal consistency improved fake-news classification on benchmark data
items.streamSummary: MLCL combined text, images, and cross-modal consistency signals for fake-news detection and improved benchmark accuracy relative to comparison methods. The gain shows value in modeling whether modalities support one another, but the study does not establish reliability against live adversarial content or prove that a classifier can adjudicate complex claims without source verification.

items.streamTitle: REPMUS tested uncrewed anti-submarine and underwater-infrastructure surveillance at multinational scale
items.streamSummary: The Royal Navy reported that REPMUS 2026 tested underwater gliders, uncrewed surface vessels, sonar systems, sonobuoys, and allied platforms in anti-submarine and infrastructure-surveillance scenarios. The event demonstrated multinational integration and realistic experimentation, not validated combat effectiveness. Detection quality, network resilience, and human workload remain important follow-on measures.

items.streamTitle: DARPA selected Xint to study autonomous AI security analysis for military messaging software
items.streamSummary: Xint announced DARPA selection to research autonomous AI application security across messaging software used in military communications. The company cited early vulnerability findings as evidence of capability. The program is a research effort, not proof that automated analysis reduces operational cyber risk. Confirmation quality, remediation, and false-positive burden will determine practical value.

items.streamTitle: Breathing–action synchrony did not reliably change intentional binding
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Reports experiment tested whether synchronizing breathing with action changes intentional binding, a common proxy for sense of agency. The predicted effect was not reliably observed. The null result is useful because it limits a plausible embodied-cognition account rather than forcing a positive mechanism story from related physiological evidence.

items.streamTitle: LACE improved automated algorithm design on selected optimization benchmarks
items.streamSummary: A Nature Machine Intelligence paper introduced LACE, a method for automated algorithm design. It improved performance on selected optimization benchmarks, demonstrating that structured search can discover useful algorithmic strategies. The result remains benchmark-dependent: transfer, compute cost, and robustness to changed problem assumptions should accompany claims of general algorithmic improvement.
